chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khallid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in prayer wearing a qamis (tunic) without a rida' (upper garment) over it, so he said: 'It is not appropriate except that he have a rida' or an 'imamah (headscarf) with which he covers himself.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum clothing requirement for a man leading prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the aesthetic and dignified standards for the Imam leading congregational prayer, moving beyond mere validity to include propriety (adab). The requirement for an upper garment (rida') or head covering ('imamah) reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam's visible dignity and completeness of attire, distinguishing the leader's appearance from that of a mere participant. This ruling underscores the principle that the public act of worship should be performed with a level of modesty and presentation befitting the role of leadership.
